messages:
maria.s: Heads-up — customer 'Acme' reported failures after our latest envelope key rotation. App logs show AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when the worker assumes the cross-account role to decrypt the data key. Started ~2026-02-12 18:03 UTC.
ashok: Can you paste the exact error and the role ARN used?
maria.s: Error from app: `OperationAborted: Access denied for kms:Decrypt` and a shorter SDK trace: `aws.kms.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/infra-worker-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444455556666:key/abcd-1234`
maria.s: Role ARN is arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/infra-worker-role/session (cross-account assume from tenant account into our infra account). The KMS key is in infra account 444455556666.
ashok: Ok. Did we rotate the CMK and replace the grants? If a grant existed for the old key ARN it might not apply after rotation. Also check that the key policy allows the principal (the assumed role) or the role is in a statement that delegates kms:Decrypt.
jen.k: Also check EncryptionContext. If the app is setting EncryptionContext during Encrypt and not supplying the same on Decrypt, KMS will reject with AccessDenied. Do we see mismatched context in logs?
maria.s: Good call. I grepped logs — encrypt call sets EncryptionContext: `{ "env": "prod", "tenant": "acme" }`. Decrypt request from worker shows no EncryptionContext in the outgoing request (SDK v2). Suspect we missed passing context after rotation of the envelope wrapper code.
ashok: That explains it if KMS policy or grant restricts by EncryptionContext. But the core issue still: why did role-level permissions suddenly fail? Could be key policy tightened to require explicit principals. Paste key policy?
maria.s: Key policy (redacted):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAccountAdmins",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowInfraRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/infra-worker-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:tenant": "acme"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
maria.s: Note the Principal is the role (not the sts assumed principal). We thought that would be fine.
ashok: It should be, but cross-account assume will result in an assumed-role principal ARN `arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/infra-worker-role/session` which is acceptable when the key policy references the role ARN (not assumed). However, if the role is assumed via an external ID or session policy that restricts kms:Decrypt, it could deny. Also check if there's a condition on aws:SourceAccount or kms:CallerAccount that no longer matches due to assume-from-account flow.
jen.k: Another angle: Did we create an explicit grant on the old CMK that allowed the account 111122223333? Grants are not copied on key rotation (you need to recreate). If the app relied on a grant instead of a key policy or IAM, rotation would break decrypts.
maria.s: We did have a grant earlier for the worker principal. I can't find the grant on the new key id when I run `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/acme-data-key --region us-west-2`. It returns empty.
ashok: There you go. Short-term fix: re-create the grant pointing to the role ARN and include Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey as needed. Longer-term: prefer key policy + IAM allow or ensure your rekey rotation automation recreates grants.
jen.k: If you recreate a grant, remember some SDKs require a grant token on Decrypt when the grant is brand new and the requester used the grant to encrypt. If you get GrantTokenMissing, supply the grant token to the decrypt call or wait a few seconds for eventual consistency.
sec-bot: [alert] KMS key rotation event recorded for key/abcd-1234 at 2026-02-12T17:59:02Z. Automated note: grants were not propagated by rotation script.
infra-bot: Ran a quick IAM policy simulator: role/infra-worker-role has explicit Allow for kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444455556666:key/abcd-1234, but simulation fails when EncryptionContext condition is missing.
maria.s: Action plan: 1) Recreate grant for infra-worker-role as emergency fix (will do now). 2) Patch worker to forward EncryptionContext on Decrypt calls. 3) Update rotation playbook to recreate grants and validate EncryptionContext invariants. 4) Add automated post-rotation smoke test that runs a round-trip encrypt/decrypt.
ashok: +1. For (1) use `aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/infra-worker-role --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey` and capture `GrantId` and `GranteePrincipal`.
jen.k: I'll open a short PR to pass EncryptionContext through the wrapper. Also add an invariant check in our tests.
maria.s: Done with grant recreation — app decrypts now. Leaving remediation ticket for rotation playbook updates. Thanks team :thumbsup:
